checks: Rescaling u to unit length leaves the ratio and the product of width sums and reciprocal widths unchanged. A,B have positive widths and their interior projection levels have full (d-1)-dimensional sections.

The sum of the two sections at the same relative position s lies in the actual sum section at relative position s. Translating the two parallel affine hyperplanes to the common direction space permits the ordinary (d-1)-dimensional Brunn–Minkowski bound. The last estimate by f(s)+g(s) is valid also for d=2, where it is algebraically equal.

The Fubini differential for the sum section is (w_A+w_B)ds, and for each endpoint it is its own width times ds. Thus the volume bound is a(2+R+R^(-1)), and division by a relates it to 2^d|M|/a. The two weaker ratio bounds follow without dropping a necessary hypothesis.

Matched 8407bedf6b42ff39 §4 (9) and the weaker oblique-segment estimates of f968b5a47e83bb95 §1 (5). The proof uses full Minkowski sections and requires no support segment parallel to the chosen normal.

overlap.comparison: That result uses d-dimensional Brunn–Minkowski on complementary endpoint caps. It does not give a constraint on directional widths from the volume of the uncut Minkowski sum.

readability: The d=1 sentence proves the two separate comparisons only. The stronger displayed joint ratio inequality is restricted to d>=2.
review_method: Independent cold proof read of the frozen statement and proof, followed by source and exact dependency comparison and exact rational checks where applicable.
summary: Sections taken at a common relative height yield the two-sided width-ratio constraint in dimensions at least two. Equal-length intervals give the separate d=1 comparisons directly.
